candidate_additions: Assigns ERG28 a non-catalytic scaffold role in the sterol C4-demethylation complex and links it to SREBP-2 regulation.
Adds RDH11 as an SREBP-2-regulated hepatic cholesterol-homeostasis gene.
Specifies MTTP–ACAT2 coupling between cholesterol esterification and VLDL export.
Identifies Ddr2, Cetn2, Zfp839, and Tas2r138 as lacking pathway evidence.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Changes the pathway description from complete to nearly complete.
No longer explicitly interprets SCAP, INSIG1, and LDLR perturbation directions as knockout-dependent suppression, hyperactivation, and compensatory induction.
Weakens the claim that reduced DGAT2/MTTP activity directly attenuates upstream cholesterol biosynthesis and instead emphasizes broader lipid-export coupling.
Drops the claim that the SCAP–INSIG1–LDLR circuit gates the program in both young and aged hepatocytes.
decision_relevant_differences: ACAT2 is reassigned from an early HMG-CoA-generating role in the baseline to cholesterol esterification in the candidate.
ERG28 and RDH11 receive specific functional assignments that expand the program beyond catalytic pathway enzymes.
The candidate is more cautious about pathway completeness and the causal interpretation of perturbation effects.
assessment.rationale: Both annotations identify P21 as a hepatocyte mevalonate-to-cholesterol biosynthesis program controlled by SCAP–INSIG1–SREBP2 and coupled to acetyl-CoA supply and DGAT2/MTTP-dependent lipid export. The candidate preserves that central interpretation but meaningfully refines individual gene roles, especially ACAT2, ERG28, and RDH11, while weakening some causal and perturbation-direction claims.
shared_core_conclusions: P21 represents de novo hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis through the mevalonate and post-squalene pathways.
SCAP–INSIG1-dependent SREBP-2 signaling transcriptionally regulates the program, with LDLR representing the uptake/homeostasis arm.
ACSS2 supplies acetyl-CoA for lipid and cholesterol synthesis.
DGAT2 and MTTP connect the sterol program to triglyceride handling, VLDL assembly, and MASLD-related lipid metabolism.
